7783.stem: A bag contains 11 red lollies and 5 blue lollies. Sarah takes a lolly from the bag without looking and eats it. She then takes another without looking and eats it.

figures.cap: solution sketch: hand-drawn tree diagram with branch probabilities

parts.latex: What is the probability Sarah will choose a blue lolly for her first choice?
By drawing a tree diagram, find the probability that Sarah eats two lollies of different colours.

solutions.latex:
There are $5$ blue lollies among $16$ in total.
$$P(B) = \dfrac{5}{16}$$

\exfigure{708_q19_s1}

The lollies are eaten, so the second pick is without replacement. Different colours means $RB$ or $BR$.
$$\begin{aligned} P(RB) &= \dfrac{11}{16} \times \dfrac{5}{15} = \dfrac{11}{48} \\ P(BR) &= \dfrac{5}{16} \times \dfrac{11}{15} = \dfrac{11}{48} \end{aligned}$$
$$\begin{aligned} P(BR \text{ or } RB) &= \dfrac{11}{48} + \dfrac{11}{48} \\ &= \dfrac{11}{24} \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ P(\text{different colours}) = \dfrac{11}{24}$$
